_comment: Guided tour of the native converter. 'name' is the emtk control (a spec action, or the history table).

steps.title: What you pick decides the direction
steps.text: There is no pack/unpack switch. The Input table lists the photon streams of the workspace (files dropped on the ChiSurf window land there). Pick a vendor file (.ptu, .spc, .ht3) and it is packed into a .pto; pick a stream of a .pto and its container is unpacked back out to the vendor files and results it holds. Select one or more rows, then press Use selected.

await.hint: Select a photon stream and press Use selected (Load example adds one to the workspace first).

steps.title: Nothing is ever deleted
steps.text: Packing writes the .pto beside the vendor file and keeps the original, then checks the container against its checksum. Unpacking writes the vendor files back and keeps the container. Either direction can be repeated or thrown away with no loss, and every conversion becomes a row of this table; what was written appears in the workspace under what it came from.

steps.title: Files dropped together are one measurement
steps.text: A recording split across m000.spc, m001.spc, ... is one measurement, so streams used together are packed into one .pto, in file-name order. The row lists them in that order.

steps.title: The .set rides along, never leads
steps.text: A Becker & Hickl .set is an .spc's sidecar. Next to its .spc it is picked up automatically with the file it belongs to; offered alone it is Rejected: it is not a measurement, it is the header of one.

steps.title: Tidy up
steps.text: Clear history removes the finished rows from the list. It never touches a file on disk.
